transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-09 15:30 PDT
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marcus Lopez (Redwood Product), Dr. Elena Rivera (Amplify Head of ML), Samir Gupta (Amplify SRE), Carly Nguyen (Amplify PM), Tom Brooks (Amplify Legal)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, brief):
Amplify is scoping a 6-week POC to validate open-model options for a lab-notes extraction and QA augmentation workload across 3 languages (EN/ES/FR). Key success criteria: 95% extraction F1 on clinical fields, <120ms p50 latency for 1-2 token generations in hosted pilot or acceptable 300ms p50 in dedicated, and cost target ~ $0.0007/token equivalent via batching/cache. Action: Redwood to propose 3 model candidates + bench harness; Amplify to provide sample data.

Topics covered:
- POC goals & success criteria
- Workload profile (qps, concurrency, average context length)
- Model shortlist and quality tradeoffs (open models)
- Multilingual/domain adaptation considerations and few-shot prompt design
- Benchmark plan, observable metrics, and timeline
- Security/compliance constraints (data residency, KMS, SOC 2)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. Quick roll call — we got Elena, Samir, Carly, Tom from Amplify. And from our side Priya, Marcus and myself. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Dr. Elena Rivera (Amplify): Good, thanks. Excited to get into the model choices. We've got a bit of a time box — leadership wants a POC that proves quality and cost math within six weeks.
[00:20] Priya Shah (Redwood SE): Great. Before we jump into models, can we confirm the workload shape? Elena I know you sent an email but just to be explicit: expected peak qps for the pilot vs expected steady state?
[00:32] Dr. Elena Rivera: For pilot we expect 40 qps bursty, think 15 sustained qps. Production could be 300 qps later but not part of this POC. Most requests are short prompts ~ 150-400 tokens input, output usually concise extraction snippets 20-60 tokens.
[00:47] Samir Gupta (Amplify SRE): Also we need to know concurrency — we'll probably have 8 concurrent workers hitting the endpoint during integration tests. And latency target is important — we want sub-200-ish for interactive flows, but we can accept higher for batch.
[01:05] Marcus Lopez (Redwood Product): Noted. For benching we'll model 8 concurrent and a couple synthetic spikes to 50 qps.
[01:12] Carly Nguyen (Amplify PM): On success criteria, Elena mentioned F1 on extraction fields. Are you comfortable sharing the exact metrics?
[01:20] Dr. Elena Rivera: Yes. Primary metric is F1 on structured fields (patient id, sample id, assay result normal/abnormal) with target 0.95. Secondary is hallucination rate under 2% measured by manual spot checks. Cost per 1k tokens is the third axis we need to optimize for.
[01:36] Jordan Kim: Perfect. That gives us three axes: quality, latency, cost. Our suggestion is a short-list of open models with tradeoffs. Priya, want to run through candidates?
[01:45] Priya Shah: Sure. Given you need multilingual support EN/ES/FR and clinical domain sensitivity, my quick shortlist is: 1) Mistral-XXL-style open model (high quality but heavier compute), 2) Llama3 family variant (good balance and widely-quantized), 3) Mistral-Mix / Mosaic medium with instruction tuning for cost-sensitive paths. We also propose a distilled Redwood-curated variant (we call it RW-lite internally) for latency-sensitive routing.
[02:12] Dr. Elena Rivera: Quick question — any pre-trained clinical specialization? We don't want to fine-tune full model for the POC. Few-shot plus prompt engineering is preferred.
[02:22] Priya Shah: Correct — POC approach is few-shot and light adapter layers if needed. We won't recommend full fine-tune unless you move to pilot. We can test a small LoRA path but keep it optional.
[02:31] Samir Gupta: From infra side we have some constraints: traffic must remain inside our VPC for the dedicated pilot; for hosted we need an ingress peering and strict egress rules. Also Tom will want to review KMS and audit logs.
[02:44] Tom Brooks (Legal): Yes, SOC 2 compliance and the ability to provide an exportable audit trail is mandatory. Also we need clarification on data retention in hosted mode — can you guarantee no input retention?
[02:56] Jordan Kim: Yes, we have hosted modes that don't retain inputs and Dedicated/Private options for data residency. We'll include our SOC2 and security whitepaper in the follow-up.
[03:04] Carly Nguyen: Back to models — can you summarize expected latency & cost per candidate at our context lengths?
[03:10] Priya Shah: Very roughly: Mistral-XXL style on 8 A100-equivalents: p50 token latency ~ 70-90ms when batched; cost higher per token. Llama3-like quantized on T4/RTX-class hardware: p50 ~120-180ms with better cost. RW-lite distilled: p50 <50ms optimized for short outputs, much lower token cost but quality drop on nuanced clinical phrasing. We'll run bench permutations with/without KV caching which helps multi-turns.
[03:40] Dr. Elena Rivera: You mentioned KV cache — for extraction workflows we sometimes reuse prompt prefixes across patients; that could reduce compute, right?
[03:47] Priya Shah: Exactly. Prefix caching and deduping frequently reduces per-token work. For your workload where a large chunk of system prompt is reused, caching will cut costs significantly. We'll model that in bench.
[03:56] Jordan Kim: Let's talk benchmarking plan. Priya?
[04:00] Priya Shah: Proposal: two-phase bench. Phase A: functional accuracy bench using your masked dataset (2k examples) for F1/hallucination across three model candidates. Phase B: performance bench: throughput/latency/cost with representative request size and concurrency (8 conc, spikes to 50 qps). We'll run both hosted and dedicated-style runs to show tradeoffs.
[04:20] Dr. Elena Rivera: How long will that take? We need results within two weeks ideally.
[04:24] Priya Shah: We can generally complete Phase A in 4 business days after we get data. Phase B another 3-4 days. So two weeks is feasible if we get samples this week.
[04:33] Carly Nguyen: Ok. On anonymized samples — we can provide 2k masked records but a couple of notes: the customer ID fields are sensitive; we will mask and also provide a schema mapping. Is that enough?
[04:44] Priya Shah: Yes, schema mapping + a small README for prompt templates is ideal. We'll use the mapping for automated metric alignment.
[04:50] Samir Gupta: A heads-up on network: for hosted bench runs we will request a test VPC peering and short-lived access. How do you handle ephemeral keys?
[04:59] Jordan Kim: We support short-lived tokens, IP allowlists, and dedicated peering. We'll include a runbook in the follow-up.
[05:06] Tom Brooks: Also need to confirm encryption-at-rest and KMS controls for the dedicated offering.
[05:10] Marcus Lopez: Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS; Private on-prem includes HSM integrations. We'll put the exact matrix in the security doc.
[05:17] Dr. Elena Rivera: Good. Back to model tradeoffs — what about multilingual performance? Spanish/ French are critical for ~20% of traffic.
[05:24] Priya Shah: Most open-model families have decent multilingual coverage, but the degradation varies: Mistral-XXL tends to hold up well across Romance languages if instruction fine-tuned; Llama3 variants may need targeted few-shot examples in each language. We propose sampling the 2k set by language to ensure we test each.
[05:41] Jordan Kim: For hallucination controls we can add constrained generation patterns, JSON schema enforcement and post-processing checks. That will factor into the hallucination metric.
[05:49] Carly Nguyen: Are you suggesting schema-constrained decoding during inference? That might add latency.
[05:54] Priya Shah: Slightly, yes — but we can do a hybrid: beam-free constrained parsing in the client side plus soft constraints in the model; tradeoff is minimal latency in most candidates. We'll quantify in Phase B.
[06:06] Dr. Elena Rivera: On the cost front — your earlier note about $0.0007/token equivalent — is that realistic?
[06:12] Jordan Kim: For a production-ish profile with caching & batching it's achievable for distill-like paths. For high-quality Mistral-class models it's more like $0.0015–0.003/token. We'll surface exact numbers once benches complete.
[06:23] Samir Gupta: For the dedicated pilot we need committed throughput numbers. What's your minimum reserved capacity?
[06:29] Marcus Lopez: Typical reserved blocks start at an equivalent of ~40 qps sustained for a given model family; we can arrange a smaller dev bucket for POC but keep in mind dedicated capacity has a lead time for GPU allocation. For the POC we recommend hosted benches with dedicated pilot alignment as step 2.
[06:47] Dr. Elena Rivera: Timeline recap: you said Phase A 4 business days, Phase B 3-4, so two weeks. We need an internal steering committee update by week end — can we get a short one-pager and a ballpark cost table before then?
[07:00] Jordan Kim: Yes, I'll send a one-pager and ballpark hosted vs dedicated cost bands by tomorrow EOD.
[07:05] Tom Brooks: Please include contract-level questions — data deletion SLA, liability caps, and indemnification.
[07:10] Jordan Kim: Will do.
[07:12] Carly Nguyen: A practical question — what's the sample rate for human review you recommend for measuring hallucination? 100 examples? 500?
[07:19] Priya Shah: For a POC 200 random samples stratified by language should be enough to estimate hallucination to within a narrow CI. For production you may want continuous sampling or active sampling attached to drift alerts.
[07:31] Dr. Elena Rivera: On evaluation — will you run exact match vs fuzzy matching? Medical abbreviations often cause tokenization mismatch.
[07:38] Priya Shah: We'll run both: token-level F1 and normalized-string F1 (phone stripping, abbrev expansion). We'll share the evaluation scripts so you can reproduce.
[07:47] Samir Gupta: If we move to a dedicated pilot, what rollback/fallback options exist if a model regresses?
[07:54] Marcus Lopez: Redwood supports automatic fallback routing to a cheaper or smaller model variant and can do canary rollouts. Observability hooks let you detect regression signals and auto-route.
[08:03] Dr. Elena Rivera: Nice. One more — can you simulate worst-case latency tail (p95/p99) in the bench? That's what our UI team cares about.
[08:10] Priya Shah: Absolutely. We'll include p50/p90/p95/p99 and cold-start scenarios (KV cache miss).
[08:16] Jordan Kim: Quick clarification on deliverables: 1) Model shortlist + rationale, 2) Evaluation harness and scripts, 3) Phase A accuracy report, 4) Phase B perf & cost report, 5) Security docs and runbook. Does that match expectations?
[08:28] Dr. Elena Rivera: Yes. Please add the expected SLO numbers for each model candidate in the report.
[08:33] Jordan Kim: Noted.
[08:35] Tom Brooks: For legal review, we'll need your DPA and evidence of SOC 2. If you can provide those by Monday that helps accelerate procurement.
[08:44] Jordan Kim: We'll attach them to the follow-up email.
[08:47] Carly Nguyen: One last operational detail — we have a requirement to log inference inputs/outputs into our audit trail for debugging but need them redacted for PHI. Does Redwood support streaming logs to customer sinks?
[08:57] Priya Shah: Yes, we can forward logs to your S3/Google cloud bucket with configured redaction and also push structured metrics to your Prometheus endpoint. We'll coordinate how to set redaction rules.
[09:09] Dr. Elena Rivera: Great. Any final questions from Redwood?
[09:13] Marcus Lopez: Just timeline confirmation — we'll start the bench as soon as we get the 2k masked dataset and schema. We also need a small number of edge-case examples (maybe 50) to validate hallucination tests.
[09:25] Dr. Elena Rivera: We'll prepare that and have Samir drop it in the shared secure bucket by Wednesday.
[09:29] Jordan Kim: Perfect. To wrap up we'll send the docs (security pack, bench plan, cost bands) and book the benchmark kickoff with Infra for March 15.
[09:38] Carly Nguyen: Thanks everyone.
[09:40] Tom Brooks: Thanks.
[09:42] End of meeting.
